outputs.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Actual in-game Korean fantasy workplace-comedy comic atlas, not a slide or UI mockup. Generate one 4:3 landscape image preferably 2048x1536, EXACTLY FOUR EQUAL PANELS in a 2x2 grid, panel boundaries at 50% width and 50% height. No margins or gutters. Every quadrant will be separately displayed. No text, letters, captions, speech bubbles or watermark: runtime draws the Korean dialogue.
Reference 1 establishes the cartoon style and cast. Reference 2 establishes the main mechanic: teal hood with brass goggles, brown leather apron and gloves, toolbox, young cute chibi human. Keep identity and palette. Bright hand-inked fantasy comedy webtoon, bold clean outlines, rich flat cel shading, expressive exaggeration, squash and stretch, sweat drops and surprise marks. Teal stone dungeon, brass floor traps, orange torches. Friendly non-gory cartoon skeleton guards with red-tabarded light armor and helmets. The hero is a handsome blond armored adventurer with a red cape: show him genuinely COOL, heroic and dramatically lit; humor comes from the mess he leaves and exhausted employees.
CRITICAL COMPOSITION IN EACH PANEL: upper 28% remains quiet wall, sky or light for two runtime speech balloons. No faces, hands or key action in the upper 28%. Left speaker occupies lower-left-middle around x=28%, right speaker lower-right-middle around x=75%. Keep essential props/actions visible in middle 35%-85%. Use full complete scenes rather than disconnected icons.
ACT ONE, panels in reading order:
TOP LEFT (1) — THE HERO ARRIVES: The hero on the LEFT makes a spectacular entrance through immense open dungeon doors, gleaming sword held diagonally low, sweeping red cape, powerful heroic stance, luminous backlight and sparkles. On the RIGHT a nervous skeleton sentry grips a tiny spear with trembling knees. The dungeon is still intact: working brass floor traps and guard posts. Dynamic epic low-angle entrance but keep heads below the 28% balloon zone.
TOP RIGHT (2) — HE CONQUERS THE DUNGEON: Hero on LEFT performs a dazzling sword slash, golden arc travelling across the middle of the scene, confidently smashing a mechanical trap. Brass gears and stone fragments fly. The skeleton on RIGHT comically tumbles apart into separated clean cartoon bones with a shocked detached skull, never gore. Energetic comic action, visible broken traps. Show actual conquest, not another standing portrait.
BOTTOM LEFT (3) — HE LEAVES IN GLORY: Hero on LEFT proudly strides back up the exit stairs into glorious daylight, red cape billowing and a small treasure pouch in hand, heroic satisfied profile. On RIGHT the same skeleton's skull sits on a pile of its own bones among wrecked traps, looking after him in disbelief. The room is visibly thoroughly wrecked. NO mechanic in these first three panels.
BOTTOM RIGHT (4) — THE REAL PROTAGONIST SHUFFLES IN: The teal-hooded mechanic enters from LEFT, trudging with slumped shoulders and very tired half-lidded eyes, dragging a brown toolbox along the ground; small dust puffs and heavy footsteps. Mechanic stares at the huge mess, conveys 'overtime again'. On RIGHT the cheerful skeleton skull perches on a crate amid its bones, greeting the mechanic. Strong comic contrast between a heroic arrival and an exhausted employee arrival.

ACT TWO, four panels in reading order. ADD THE DEMON LORD BOSS: a comically pompous broad short demon with a purple face, two curved black horns, a small gold crown, extravagant crimson cape over black-and-gold armor. Very expressive bushy eyebrows and little fangs. He holds a clipboard or points at a pocket watch. Looks like an annoying middle manager, not a horror monster. The same exact boss must recur in panels 1 and 3 of this atlas.
TOP LEFT (5) — BOSS CHEWS OUT THE MECHANIC: Demon lord BOSS on LEFT looms dramatically, one hand pointing to his pocket watch, other holding a long damage checklist, cheeks puffed in impatient scolding. Mechanic on RIGHT hunches, sweats, grips a wrench and toolbox, eyes dead with exhaustion. Broken traps around them. A tiny skull peeks behind the mechanic but only two main speakers. Comedic workplace nagging, no violence.
TOP RIGHT (6) — OVERTIME REPAIR WITH A SKELETON: Mechanic on LEFT kneels and installs a brass gear component into a floor trap, visibly tired but working. On RIGHT a half-reassembled friendly skeleton sits on a workbench, holding up its own detached BARE SKELETAL FOOT to offer help as if it were a hand; the foot's toes and heel are unmistakable. Both react to the ridiculous mistake. Piles of bones, tools, repaired gears. Warm work sparks.
BOTTOM LEFT (7) — THE BOSS ADDS MORE WORK: Same demon lord BOSS on LEFT points toward an open doorway showing another wrecked room, holding an absurdly long rolled-out checklist and giving a smug 'one more thing' smile. Mechanic on RIGHT has finally finished a small repaired trap and looks devastated, mouth wide open, giant sweat drops; a newly rebuilt skeleton guard stands proudly in the middle background. Visible contrast: this room repaired, next room wrecked. The boss is impatiently assigning another room.
BOTTOM RIGHT (8) — INTO THE FIRST ASSIGNMENT: Mechanic on LEFT, exhausted but determined, holds the toolbox and wrench and walks toward an open doorway into the next repair room. On RIGHT the fully reassembled friendly skeleton soldier enthusiastically volunteers to help, proudly holding out its own detachable arm like a spare tool, cheeky smile. Mechanic gives an incredulous sideways glance. Behind them: restored trap and a lit exit; through the doorway: scattered trap parts waiting for repair. A small high window shows moonlight, indicating overtime. End as a comic buddy moment leading into gameplay, not a triumphant final ending.
